event.summary: Deletion treats unavailable Podman executable as confirmed cleanup
event.detail:
Reviewed commit: 04d85f0c98a9b635709d00b056719a0baa7fd3fc.

TLDR: deleting a retired container session may forget the session when Podman cannot be resolved, potentially leaving its container behind.

Details: container.rs:170-190 passes missing resolution as None, skips engine commands and clears the initialization marker. service/teardown.rs:533-590 reconstructs the retired runtime, holds its permanent flock, revokes creation and calls remove before proceeding with process cleanup and eventual row deletion. scope.rs:1233-1281 searches absolute PATH entries for a regular executable with a UTF-8 path, returning None if none resolves; a resolved executable's spawn, command or storage failures remain errors unless a subsequent exists command confirms absence with status 1. The new behavior deliberately differs from the prior eager executable requirement. A container could outlive removal of its executable; no such runtime state was exercised.

Suggested bucket: other for the established cleanup consequence; could-be-highest if orphaning loses user-owned processes/work, which the inspected source does not establish. Confidence: confirmed source behavior, not an observed runtime failure. proposed_drop: exact explicit specification acceptance. SPEC.md:4816-4823, Retired containerized sessions, says: 'Delete retains the legacy container-removal path and confirms absence. Missing Podman counts as nothing left to remove.' SPEC_impl.md:8651-8655, Rootless Podman sessions, says: 'Resolve Podman lazily. A host without Podman has nothing left to remove. Other unconfirmed cleanup keeps the session for retry.' Both contracts remain at 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333 (SPEC.md:4910-4917; SPEC_impl.md:8439-8453), whose assigned container.rs change only broadens a comment from private to any inherited tmux coordinates; the environment-removal loop is unchanged.

Recorded as a finding with proposed_drop for independent checking because the potential strongest consequence is accepted only by specification. Original suspected orphaned-container consequence is preserved. possible_cover: none; coverage sources were not consulted. Checks: complete assigned patches, full replacement source, resolver, teardown caller, prior creator lock/ticket contract, and pinned retirement contracts read. No runtime tests or reproductions performed. No unresolved source check remains for this proposed drop.

event.summary: PATH lookup failure is broader than genuine Podman absence
event.detail:
Reviewed commit: 04d85f0c98a9b635709d00b056719a0baa7fd3fc.

TLDR: deleting a retired container session can skip container cleanup and forget its handle when the supervisor cannot find Podman, even though the engine may still be installed. Original consequence retained: a container and its user-owned processes/work may be orphaned.

Details: container.rs:170-190 treats every None from scope::resolve_program as cleanup success. scope.rs:1233-1281 returns None for an unset PATH, an installed executable omitted from PATH, relative-only search entries, metadata failures (all errors, not just NotFound), nonexecutable/nonregular candidates and non-UTF-8 candidate paths. This is not proof that Podman is absent from the host. A resolved executable that fails to spawn or run does produce a cleanup error, so the distinction is specifically pre-spawn resolution failure.

Exact acceptance: SPEC.md:4820-4821 says 'Delete retains the legacy container-removal path and confirms absence. Missing Podman counts as nothing left to remove.' SPEC_impl.md:8652-8654 says 'Resolve Podman lazily. A host without Podman has nothing left to remove. Other unconfirmed cleanup keeps the session for retry.' Those sentences literally accept genuine missing-engine cleanup, but do not explicitly equate PATH omission or metadata inspection failure with a host without Podman. scope.rs:1245-1257 does explicitly document unsupported non-UTF-8 tool paths as absent; that narrower documented case must not silently authorize every other failure.

Suggested bucket: other on established cleanup/handle consequence; could-be-highest if an established shipped route loses user processes/work; this strongest premise is not established. Confidence: confirmed resolver branch distinction, remaining consequence/contract interpretation under investigation. proposed_drop: partial only, for genuine engine absence under the quoted specification; blanket drop of PATH/metadata ambiguity is no longer proposed. possible_cover: caller reports likely same lazy-missing-engine claim as g001/f2; no external finding file or coverage metadata read.

Next source checks: determine whether startup guarantees a PATH containing any previously used Podman, whether old tickets retain resolved executable coordinates, and whether legacy creator revocation or subsequent scope cleanup independently proves container absence. No experiments or reproductions performed.

event.summary: PATH lookup failure is broader than genuine Podman absence
event.detail:
Reviewed commit: 04d85f0c98a9b635709d00b056719a0baa7fd3fc.

TLDR: deleting a retired container session can skip container removal and forget its handle when the supervisor cannot find Podman, even though the engine may still be installed. Original suspected consequence retained: a container and its user-owned processes/work may be orphaned.

Details: container.rs:170-190 maps every None from scope::resolve_program into cleanup success. scope.rs:1233-1281 returns None for unset PATH, an installed executable omitted from PATH, relative-only search entries, metadata failures of any kind, nonexecutable/nonregular candidates and non-UTF-8 candidate paths. In particular the metadata match at scope.rs:1266-1268 erases inspection errors instead of preserving an unconfirmed result. None proves only no accepted candidate in this process's search path, not a host without Podman. Errors after a path resolves remain retryable unless a subsequent exists command confirms absence with status 1.

Caller route: service/teardown.rs:533-590 holds the creation flock, revokes the ticket and calls remove before ordinary process cleanup; if other cleanup succeeds, teardown.rs:999-1002 removes the session row. No later engine-absence check exists on that route. service/sweep.rs:1410-1564 only checks/kills scopes and process identities; it contains no Podman call or storage-removal/absence check. Even if its signals stop a live container, that is not removal of an already-stopped container's storage. The old creator contract (parent revision container.rs:1-6,484-522,569-573) deliberately placed creation outside agent containment, optionally in its own scope, and stored the absolute Podman path in CreationTicket.runtime.podman (parent lines 31-47). The new cleanup unlinks that ticket at container.rs:160-164 and never reads that known path. Revocation prevents delayed helpers from newly creating a container; it does not prove an existing container disappeared. The permanent-inode source refutation in c2 remains valid for creation after Delete, with this narrowed meaning.

Startup checks: main.rs:2172-2199 delegates to service::run; core.rs:18851-18900 starts the owned runtime and constructor; core.rs:6345-6383,6429-6520 processes startup overrides and validates Farhelm/state paths without restoring a prior Podman path. Targeted PATH searches in the supervisor constructor/service and CLI plus a complete set_var search over supervisor source and main.rs found no process PATH replacement. The resolver reads the current inherited supervisor PATH, not the agent login-shell environment or the retired ticket's resolved path. These checks do not prove an affected installation has actually changed PATH.

Exact acceptance: SPEC.md:4820-4821 says 'Delete retains the legacy container-removal path and confirms absence. Missing Podman counts as nothing left to remove.' SPEC_impl.md:8652-8654 says 'Resolve Podman lazily. A host without Podman has nothing left to remove. Other unconfirmed cleanup keeps the session for retry.' The same wording is retained at the second assigned commit 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333 (SPEC.md:4914-4915, SPEC_impl.md:8449-8451). This literally accepts genuine engine absence. It does not explicitly define an installed engine omitted from PATH, or failed metadata inspection, as genuine absence. scope.rs:1245-1257 separately documents unsupported non-UTF-8 tool paths as absent; that narrower case is documented acceptance and cannot silently broaden the rest. SPEC.md Supported host setup limits hand-written/modified service setups to best effort, so a manually damaged service PATH is not asserted as a supported automatic-upgrade regression.

Suggested bucket: other for cleanup/handle loss; could-be-highest: original possible loss of orphaned user-owned processes/work is preserved, but the strongest consequence is not established and is not used to choose the bucket. Confidence: source-confirmed branch and caller behavior; unverified after investigation as a reportable contract violation. Exact remaining premise: whether the maintainer's accepted term 'Missing Podman' intentionally includes every PATH/metadata resolution failure, and whether a supported deployed host retains old container state while hitting that branch. Source settles the implementation distinction but contains no explicit acceptance for all those cases and cannot establish historical operator environments. A maintainer interpretation or a supported deployment's retained path/container evidence would settle those premises; no runtime investigation was requested or performed.

proposed_drop: partial only for genuine engine absence and documented unsupported non-UTF-8 locations under the quoted rules; no blanket proposed drop for other PATH/metadata ambiguity. The parent has not accepted a drop. possible_cover: caller reports likely overlap with g001/f2 on lazy missing-engine removal and specified Delete acceptance; preserve this ID and the narrower ambiguity for parent synthesis. No other group's findings or coverage sources read. Suggested fix direction if ambiguity is not accepted: preserve a resolution-error category and retain the row on inspection errors; do not infer installation-wide absence from failure to find a command on the supervisor PATH. No experiments, reproductions, tests or builds performed. All readily checkable source premises pursued; no uninvestigated source lead remains.

event.summary: PATH lookup failure is broader than genuine Podman absence
event.detail:
Reviewed commit: 04d85f0c98a9b635709d00b056719a0baa7fd3fc.

TLDR: deleting a retired container session can skip container removal and forget its handle when the supervisor cannot find Podman although the engine may remain installed. Original possible consequence retained: orphaned container storage or user-owned processes/work. No process survival, credential exposure or extra loss of work beyond the requested Delete is established.

Details: container.rs:170-190 treats None from scope::resolve_program as successful cleanup. scope.rs:1233-1281 returns None for missing/unusable PATH entries and any metadata failure, not proof of installation-wide absence. teardown.rs:570-590 revokes creation under its permanent flock, then runs ordinary process cleanup; :999-1002 deletes the row if the other steps pass. sweep.rs:1410-1564 checks processes/scopes and does not remove or inspect Podman storage. Creation revocation prevents future ticket consumption but does not prove removal of existing state. Existing stopped-container storage is the narrow cleanup consequence; strongest process/work consequences remain conditional.

Discovery-turn premise resolution requested by parent: checked actual pre-retirement producer, not just CreationTicket's type. 04d85f0c^ service/core.rs:9553-9557 calls container::preflight in supervisor request validation. More decisively, :17271-17303 constructs ContainerRuntime and calls container::executable at :17276 inside the supervisor's launch construction, before serializing LaunchSpec or starting the shim. Parent container.rs:101-107 resolves through scope::resolve_program; publish at :500-509 stores that already-resolved runtime in CreationTicket. Therefore the absolute Podman path came from the old supervisor's own inherited PATH, not an agent login shell. The agent login environment cannot supply a hidden engine that the same supervisor could not initially resolve. This disproves that proposed ordinary same-startup shipped producer; it does not establish PATH stability across a later supervisor restart, or rule out a later metadata inspection error. No supported automatic transition changing that PATH has been demonstrated.

Current startup sources checked in the previous turn (main.rs:2172-2199; core.rs:6345-6383,6429-6520,18851-18900) neither read the old ticket's executable nor restore a previous Podman PATH. Complete supervisor/main set_var search found no process PATH replacement. A supported deployed environment's historical PATH transition is still not established from that fact alone. The old ticket's absolute path is discarded by revocation, but using it would be a possible implementation choice, not an established requirement.

Exact acceptance retained: SPEC.md:4820-4821 says 'Delete retains the legacy container-removal path and confirms absence. Missing Podman counts as nothing left to remove.' SPEC_impl.md:8652-8654 says 'Resolve Podman lazily. A host without Podman has nothing left to remove. Other unconfirmed cleanup keeps the session for retry.' This wording persists at the second assigned commit. scope.rs:1245-1257 explicitly treats unsupported non-UTF-8 tool locations as absent. No literal rule found equates every omitted PATH entry or metadata failure with a host without Podman. Hand-edited units and manual remote supervisor setups are best effort under SPEC.md:5251-5283, so such edits are not asserted to prove a guaranteed automatic-upgrade regression.

Suggested bucket: other for unconfirmed resource cleanup and record loss. Could-be-highest: original orphaned-process/work possibility retained for independent judgment, but not established; Delete already authorizes destruction of the container and its internal files, and later process cleanup may stop it. Confidence: confirmed source route and newly resolved producer premise; unverified after investigation as a reportable contract violation. Exact missing premises remain whether 'Missing Podman' intentionally includes every pre-spawn lookup failure, and a supported deployment retaining a legacy container while hitting an unaccepted failure. Source proves old supervisor-PATH origin, not historical deployment environments or the maintainer's unstated interpretation. Retained deployment PATH/container evidence or an explicit acceptance interpretation would settle those premises; no reproduction requested/performed.

proposed_drop: partial only for genuine engine absence and documented unsupported non-UTF-8 locations under the exact quoted exceptions; no blanket drop of PATH/metadata ambiguity accepted by parent. No lowering of established strongest impact. possible_cover: discovery-neighbours.json provides g001/f2 with the same lazy missing-engine cleanup/row-loss route, likely duplicate; preserve l1 for parent reconciliation. Adjacent old-terminal guarded-Delete findings are distinct, already recorded by their owners, and are not new discoveries here. All prior source references, consequences and caveats remain preserved in this event history. No new ID or newly verified bug in this premise check; source-only analysis, no execution.

Reviewed commit: 04d85f0c98a9b635709d00b056719a0baa7fd3fc.
